title: Fishing Report - November 2.. November..crazy. | Channel 6-8
markdown:
# Fishing Report - November 2.. November..crazy.

Had a scoop or 2 of minnows left from yeaterday and the bay was near flat so across the bay we went to get back on the perch. Right to the waypoint, on plane all the way there. Drop achor at a smidge after 2pm, send the bait down with the safety off ready for the slightest tap..and waited..and waited...still waiting..WTF.  
pulled the achor and reset 7,8,9 times, casting and draging off all side of the boat trying to get a sign and not a single hit. Buddy finally pinns a hit and it goes airborn immediately. Huge bronze bomber.. Snapped off at the boat.  
Keep picking up and dropping and nothing..I finally gets a hit and I lays into! Right to the top of the water instantly, another big smallie.. Popped free at the boat.  
With a little over an hr left and no sign of perch I makes the call to get on the pike troll to see whats going on.  
Set out some baits on inline boards, set the speed to 3.5mph. Not even 2mins and one of the reels is screaming. Bronze back again! WTH!! This time we used the net and on to the scale[![20261102\_164712.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/73/73225-59f87cfc2c4f212d5937633c88401248.jpg?hash=_DSJ7T8Bnt "20261102_164712.webp")](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/20261102_164712-webp.128169/)[![20261102\_164821.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/73/73226-3803a5fca183c9bd604f0a933e0be67a.jpg?hash=ckaO21dNks "20261102_164821.webp")](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/20261102_164821-webp.128170/).  
Continue on with the troll and out of the jumbo smallies and pin a decent pike about 1/3mile from yesterday's hot spot[![20261102\_170858.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/73/73227-e00b4dafdce2308ccfdb8cd2f57af187.jpg?hash=szv27FuXxI "20261102_170858.webp")](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/20261102_170858-webp.128171/)..then another..then another.."this dont feel pike-ish or bassy". Get it top side and what a surprise,[![20261102\_172501.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/73/73228-38faecea9c96120013a45200e5bc8b09.jpg?hash=DvRo7i38WP "20261102_172501.webp")](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/20261102_172501-webp.128172/) 24" walleye.  
Zero perch on the day despite our best effort. pulled a couple fish in the closing hr, iced the the pike and the eye. Bronze back released. all 3 fat ass bass were of the same caliber. Didnt catch or hook a single smallie yesterday yet today we tied into 3 of the biggest smallies I seen all year .  
The rich diverse waters of LPB👌🏽.  
10-17fow.

Note: had no problem taking a glass boat with inboard motor through the channel at Nanticoke. Stay in the middle of the creek until the break wall of rocks starts then get close, about 20-25ft off the rocks all the way passed the lighthouse,4fow all the way through to the lake. Dont forget on your way back in stay close to the rocks until the steel break wall starts then start getting back to the middle.

 

Crazy how those schools of perch are here today, gone tomorrow....keeps it interesting for sure.

Another great day to be on the water [@SIX-GRAND](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/6959/)  
Those are some beast bronzebacks for sure ...glad you were able to get the pike and eye in the mix too. Always a good read my friend. 🐟🎣🦈

title: Fishing Report - Oct 31 & Nov1. LPB mixed bag. | Channel 6-8
markdown:
# Fishing Report - Oct 31 & Nov1. LPB mixed bag.

 

Those pike look a little cramped in the mini ⚰️... 😁

Putting on the miles and stacking up fish... I've been itching to get back out... Good fishing bud...

 

[![Three Bouys](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/avatars/m/0/99.jpg?1366217360)](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/three-bouys.99/)

Couple of nice pike [@SIX-GRAND](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/6959/) We tried for some perch on Saturday but they were lock jaw and kept 2 nice keepers. Wasn’t enough for a meal but Remi had a good taste of fresh perch  
[![IMG\_9782.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/73/73220-95137e14c79504647131923bc71208eb.jpg?hash=xWPlWYexDT "IMG_9782.webp")](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/img_9782-webp.128159/)

 

> Oct 31: Decided to give the inner bay a rest and look and get on perch elsewhere so we went pike trolling. 35-40min ride from Nanticoke to the rich waters off of the long point. Couple F18 and 60williams wobbler. 15-20fow 'trying' to racking the outside edge of some standing weeds.. Game one. Pike,pike, walleye..WALLEYE. kept 3 nice eater size pike, the eye and tossed back 2 tournament winners..biggins![View attachment 128148](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/128148/)  
> Did a troll across the shoal and north of it for a couple eyes on the way in..produced nothing.
> 
> Nov1: water looked good to across the bay so off we went to the rich waters off the long point again in search of the perch. Arrived at a nice piece of vacant water around 2pm and started the search over some promising looking grounds we worked the day before while on the pike troll.  
> The odd tap here and a hit there but nothing to set up on until around the 10th spot. Got to papper them babys up for a little over an hr before we had to scuttle back across the bay in low light. Managed 47 for keeps, 1st and likely only large mouth of the year, a dandy specimen of a red eyed fresh water grouper, bowfin and another walleye of all things[View attachment 128152](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/128152/)[View attachment 128150](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/128150/)[View attachment 128151](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/128151/)[View attachment 128149](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/128149/).  
> Great afternoon on the bay.. wish we could have located them perch a little sooner but thats the way she goes when breaking down water looking for the "hot spot".

How was it getting out the channel at Nanticoke? Last year at this time it was bad in the middle, but someone told me to hug the south break wall and that seemed to work better. Any tips would be appreciated, I may be launching there in the next little while.

 

> How was it getting out the channel at Nanticoke? Last year at this time it was bad in the middle, but someone told me to hug the south break wall and that seemed to work better. Any tips would be appreciated, I may be launching there in the next little while.

Its getting low. Stay close to the rock wall indeed(south). Where the retaining wall ends and the rocks begin is where you want start getting close to the rock wall. The middle your sure to hit bottom.

 

> Those pike look a little cramped in the mini ⚰️... 😁
> 
> Putting on the miles and stacking up fish... I've been itching to get back out... Good fishing bud...

Lol! Wasn't the mini ⚰️ but Yeah they a little tight fitting in this one too, they were some nice pike. Should have seen the ones the got put back.. BIGGINS! well over 3ft  
Definitely burning some gas and putting miles on but what ever you know. Fishing is a harmless addiction.. Just a little costly at times. Lol.

 

> Its getting low. Stay close to the rock wall indeed(south). Where the retaining wall ends and the rocks begin is where you want start getting close to the rock wall. The middle your sure to hit bottom.

OK, thanks. Kind of the same as last year. Weather is not looking good for the next week, but hopefully that changes.

 

[![SkinnyTiller](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/avatars/m/10/10003.jpg?1754179816)](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/skinnytiller.10003/)

> ... Weather is not looking good for the next week, but hopefully that changes.

Was looking ahead too- Central basin looking grim, East basin looking bit 'rosier". Keeping🤞 for Sun (rain?) & Mon being fishable and maybe a slim shot for this Fri? All I know is I seem to be 🙏ing more lately lol

I got 12 last Saturday. Be careful, there are nets in close <40fow. Not marked well, just black posts 1 mile apart, no floats. Really hard to see if they are between you and shore, they just blend into the darkness of the trees.

who ever thought that marking nets with black posts was a good idea ? I've almost ran over them once on choppy over cast day

title: Puerto Vallarta fishing report November 2026 | Channel 6-8

# Puerto Vallarta fishing report November 2026

November is one of the best months to experience Puerto Vallarta fishing, as the Pacific waters off Mexico’s coast welcome an impressive variety of game fish. With warm ocean currents, abundant baitfish, and productive offshore grounds, anglers can expect outstanding opportunities all month long. From trophy-sized marlin and yellowfin tuna to acrobatic dorado and hard-fighting roosterfish, Banderas Bay fishing offers something for every experience level.

Whether you’re planning a family outing, a half-day excursion, or a full-day deep-sea adventure, November presents plenty of reasons to book a Puerto Vallarta fishing charter and explore these remarkable waters.[![Puerto Vallarta fishing report November 2026.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/73/73222-556489db2eecf055143dab8cbfe2b6ac.jpg?hash=6MZZ1FVkEF "Puerto Vallarta fishing report November 2026.webp")](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/puerto-vallarta-fishing-report-november-2026-webp.128163/)

Offshore Fishing: Marlin, Yellowfin Tuna & Sailfish

For anglers chasing big-game action, November brings excellent offshore fishing and some of the very best fishing we have all year long. The deep Pacific waters around Puerto Vallarta attract several prized pelagic species, making it Mexico’s number one fishing destination.

Blue and Black Marlin: The offshore drop-offs and underwater structures surrounding Banderas Bay provide habitat for powerful blue and black marlin. These impressive predators are known for their strength, speed, and spectacular aerial displays. Hooking one is an unforgettable experience that challenges even experienced anglers.

Yellowfin Tuna: November is an exciting month to target trophy yellowfin tuna. Often found around offshore banks and areas of concentrated baitfish, these powerful fish deliver long, demanding fights. Anglers hoping to land a true trophy should consider a full-day offshore trip with experienced local captains.

Sailfish: Known for their distinctive dorsal fins and incredible speed, sailfish are another exciting target. Their explosive strikes and acrobatic jumps make them a favorite among sportfishing enthusiasts, particularly those practicing catch-and-release fishing.

Inshore Fishing: Dorado, Roosterfish & More[![November fishing report Puerto Vallarta snapper.jpeg.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/73/73224-b5a6a5c9f6957068e7d2820e35a29c46.jpg?hash=7ubpCmhNUy "November fishing report Puerto Vallarta snapper.jpeg.webp")](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/november-fishing-report-puerto-vallarta-snapper-jpeg-webp.128165/)

Not every memorable fishing adventure requires traveling far offshore. The productive waters of Banderas Bay offer plenty of opportunities for anglers interested in shorter trips and diverse catches. We also offer the best fishing rates in Puerto Vallarta.

Dorado (Mahi-Mahi): November brings opportunities to encounter colorful dorado, also known as mahi-mahi. Recognized for their vibrant colors and aggressive feeding behavior, these fast-swimming fish provide exciting action on light and medium tackle.

Roosterfish: One of the region’s most recognizable inshore species, roosterfish are prized for their distinctive dorsal fins and powerful runs. Rocky coastlines, sandy beaches, and areas near river mouths can provide productive fishing opportunities.Mexico fishing report

Other species worth targeting include cubera snapper, jack crevalle, and grouper. These coastal predators offer plenty of variety for anglers looking to experience sport fishing in Puerto Vallarta without committing to a long offshore journey.

Where to Fish Around Puerto Vallarta

Choosing the right fishing grounds depends on your target species, available time, and ocean conditions.

Banderas Bay: Ideal for half-day fishing trips, the bay offers relatively sheltered waters and opportunities to target dorado, smaller tuna, roosterfish, and other inshore species.

Corbeteña Rock (La Corbetena): Located approximately 35 miles offshore, this famous underwater pinnacle attracts large pelagic predators, including marlin and yellowfin tuna. It is a popular destination for anglers seeking trophy fishing in Puerto Vallarta.

El Banco: Roughly 50 miles offshore, these legendary seamounts are known for their productive waters and potential encounters with large blue marlin, black marlin, and heavyweight tuna. Full-day excursions are generally recommended to make the most of the journey.

With productive offshore grounds, diverse inshore species, and exciting big-game opportunities, November is a fantastic time to explore the Pacific coast. Whether you’re hoping to catch a trophy marlin, battle a yellowfin tuna, or enjoy a relaxing day exploring Banderas Bay, Puerto Vallarta offers an unforgettable fishing experience.  
[![Puerto Vallarta fishing report November.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/73/73223-1c4956a295b13c6a461a3e532fbd28c9.jpg?hash=nEB7aq7B6e "Puerto Vallarta fishing report November.webp")](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/puerto-vallarta-fishing-report-november-webp.128164/)

# Oct 31st, night casting in the Detroit River for Walleye

This is a PIC from the American side fishing in one of the Detroit locations. Caught 4 of the 6 in twelve casts using Jigs. The guy lives near Beaumont Texas and a 20 plus hours drive. He came just to fish for Walleye for the week.

Also saw FB and Utube Videos of catching them by boat.

If you still got the Walleye Bug, head to the Detroit River while it's still nice weather.

[![1793578821908.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/73/73212-05074fa1af965b54ae0e60bb21c8e9c8.jpg?hash=1ZowuHxaX2 "1793578821908.webp")](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/1793578821908-webp.128144/)

 

The St Clair and Detroit Rivers are wonderful fisheries and there can be some really, really hot fishing during the season. Drove the 1 1/2hrs once to cast from shore in Courtright- started 8:30pm, first 6 casts... 5 fish. Had a smoke, finished my Timmies then had to move as someone had taken my 'lucky' spot- 6th fish on 3rd cast.... limit in less than 15 minutes. Oh boy, did that pi$$ off buddy who took my 'lucky spot' 😂 3 hrs of driving for 15 mins of fishing- BIG smile during that hour and a half back to London.

Oh boy, did that pi$$ off buddy who took my 'lucky spot' 😂 3 hrs of driving for 15 mins of fishing- BIG smile during that hour and a half back to London.

I worked for the C&O Railway back in the day, with the Office behind Imperial Oil. By taking a light and shining in the river along the wall I could see their eyes. Never fished for them then at night but a friend did. As the the C&O car ferry was there and if I lighted up the water at the ferry ramp I could see 1000's of minnows.

[![1793587120023.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/73/73213-adcf6422c3b16cc84a87fc06207a26c3.jpg?hash=u_a1lG1xmm "1793587120023.webp")](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/1793587120023-webp.128146/)

Never fished for them then at night but a friend did. As the the C&O car ferry was there and if I lighted up the water at the ferry ramp I could see 1000's of minnows.
> 
> [View attachment 128146](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/128146/)

We used to hit Lower Niagara around Queenston shore fishing after working afternoon shifts and right away we would scan with our flashlights and if you seen eyes glowing back at you knew it was going to be a good night. If you didn't see eyes you usually didn't stay long... Ripped Husky Jerks or the Bob Izumi edition Ripplin Redfin in the shallows. Things have changed and I now see some incidental catches of smaller walleye while trout fishing but back than I never seen a walleye come out of there under 7 lbs and many weighed in around 11-13 lbs

title: Well, did not expect that!!! | Channel 6-8
markdown:
# Well, did not expect that!!!

Had lines in outer LPB by 6:30, one worm harness 75ft back behind a #1 dipsy and one flicker minnow 11 in 35fow. Not many marks but managed 8 fat 18-24" walleye by 9:00. Released all but one.

At 9:15 the worm harness took a rip and I set the hook into an immovable object. Only it started to move and after a couple of minutes it came to the surface and jumped, at least the front 3ft of it came out of the water. Did not believe it at first but after another a couple more minutes confirmed that it was a muskie.

I tie my harnesses with 18lb titanium wire and saw that it had the front hook in the lower lip. Fought it for about 10 minutes up the within 15ft of the boat, then it turns and bit off the wire. All I had was the swivel and 2" of wire. It lingered behind the boat for a while then took off. It was at least 1/2 the width of my 99" wide boat. Pretty fish, and not expected on a harness.

Kept fishing until 2:15 and ended the day with 15 walleye (and a close call with a muskie), did not lose count this time. Had a couple doubles and a couple of long periods with no action. Not a lot on the finder, but the planer boards were still hitting. baits 20-25ft down in 35-55fow at 1.8-2.0mph.

# Fishing Report - Port Glasgow Wed- No Bueno, the Sequel

[![SkinnyTiller](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/avatars/m/10/10003.jpg?1754179816)](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/skinnytiller.10003/)

Little sporty this am but hooked up the trailer and lucked out with the timing launching 12:30- wind and waves were on the wane. Dropped lines over 49fow, trolled out to 70fow and turned back, ending the day at 5pm over 64fow. Wonderful day- nice trek back in with no wind and nicely spaced swell, but lousy fishing. Didn't mark anything really (bait or fish) until 60fow- isolated glimmers of fish/bait throughout water column followed by long snowstorms on the sonar. Bonus was no ramp fee as the kiosks have been removed. No takers and no sniffs even on the worms, again- looks like they may have started early and moved on already. Erieau Marina said fishing has been dead there too for couple of weeks now.

title: LPB Oct 14 | Channel 6-8
markdown:
# LPB Oct 14 | Channel 6-8

Lines in at 6:30 up at 14:00. Fished 25-45 fow to stay closer to the north shore and shelter a bit from wind. Still pretty bumpy with waves very close together making boat control a little tough.

First fish at 8:15 then 8 to the boat by 9:05. Fish came in bunches, with nothing for up to an hour then a flurry of double headers and singles, then nothing again. Dragged harnesses behind jet divers and dipsys and deep and medium cranks at 1.8-2.4mph. Best was husky jerks 12 and flicker minnow 11 from 125 to 150 behind inline boards. Got several on an old Smithwick deep rouge that was running around 15-20 ft deep.

Lots of bait around but the hits came when the screen was mostly blank. Water was 58-60F with a bit of floating weed. Ended the day with 20-25 fish from 17-27" long. Just kept three goldilocks fish with the right size and shape 20-24". Only saw three or four other boats all day.

Weather is not looking good for at least a week, so we will see how it goes.

# Off Topic - Channel 6-8: Early response to the PHP security issue

**Channel 6-8: Early response to the PHP security issue**

You may have seen news reports about two serious security flaws in PHP, the software that helps run this forum. Under certain conditions, these flaws could allow an attacker to run code on a vulnerable server without logging in.

For background:  
[Associated Press: Rush is on to patch a software vulnerability that could impact 70% of websites worldwide](https://apnews.com/article/a0af9576808a0963efca8df14d4b5183)

**Channel 6-8 identified the security announcement and acted promptly. The fixes were applied to our server on October 21, 2026, by 12:49 p.m. Eastern time—the same day PHP released them.**

We first tested the update on our local test installation, then installed Ubuntu’s security-patched PHP packages on the live OVH server. The web services were restarted so the fixes took effect.

Checks afterward confirmed that the forum, media, resources, and supporting services were working. A separate verification at approximately 2 p.m. confirmed that the running PHP service was using the patched software. Later that day, we also strengthened our Cloudflare firewall protection against these attacks.

This was a response to an early security warning, rather than a repair prompted by a detected break-in.

**The treehouse explanation 🌳**

Think of Channel 6-8 as our community treehouse. PHP is part of the framework holding it together.

When the builders announced two serious weaknesses, we picked up the warning and got to work that day. These weaknesses could, under certain conditions, let someone interfere with the treehouse without a key or membership.

We tested the repairs on our practice treehouse first, then fitted the approved repairs to the real one. Afterward, we checked that the doors opened, the lights worked, and everyone could still use the treehouse. A separate inspection confirmed the repaired parts were actually in use.

Cloudflare is our lookout at the gate. We also improved its instructions to help stop suspicious visitors before they reached the treehouse.

**Was there evidence of a break-in?**

Our review of available server logs, application files, and security indicators found **no evidence of a successful compromise related to these two vulnerabilities**.

In treehouse terms, we checked the available footprints, inspected the framework, and looked for unexpected changes. We found no signs of a successful break-in through these weaknesses. That describes what our inspection found; it cannot guarantee that every possible historical event has been accounted for.

These repairs address the two vulnerabilities announced on October 21. PHP published additional configuration guidance on October 23; its applicability to our server still needs checking.

**Further information**  
[Official PHP announcement and subsequent guidance](https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-21-5)  
[Cloudflare’s explanation and protections](https://blog.cloudflare.com/php-vulnerabilities-waf-protection/)

##### Well-Known Member

*   [Oct 25, 2026](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/threads/on-the-river-this-day-out.98157/post-343879)

Went to sit on the river today with my Burwell captain for a few hours or so targetting some perch . This time of year we may hit a bunch 9-10" . Not today tho . First fish was a chunky 8.5 " perch . Next fish thought at first it was a bigger one , then all of a sudden it started peeling and peeling. Wasn't the 10" or so perch I was hoping for. Turned out to be the biggest carp I've ever caught. Bonus fight for the day . No scale to weigh it . After while Phil was reeling in his worm and something good size followed it to shore . I seen the bottom all stirred up from it , asked What it was , he didn't know but was maybe 2' long . He cast back in and boom . Got it to the net and was a nice walleye , freeked out and off it went . Damm !!! A little later he got another good hit . This time a 27.5" walleye this time in the net . Caught 4 or 5 small perch after . Was a good day out in our eyes .[![1000000198.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/73/73147-1ccd774f90295f1ac7241a8899f42675.jpg?hash=RxoWTjodos "1000000198.webp")](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/1000000198-webp.128020/)[![1000000199.webp](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/attachments/73/73148-d733c6761569e5b51b3533149803fdd3.jpg?hash=2fcDUVFqoM "1000000199.webp")](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/attachments/1000000199-webp.128021/)
